title.narrative: Ensuring the psychosocial wellbeing and mental health Of burial team members and their households

description.narrative:
This project is aimed at providing psycho-social support to the burial teams so as members of the burial team, in Sierra Leone. Sierra Leone is experiencing an outbreak of Ebola haemorrhagic fever (known as Ebola Virus Disease: EVD) which doctors have described as "unprecedented”, and it is spreading so fast and has become one of the deadliest in years. This is the first recorded outbreak of the EVD in Sierra Leone, where Lassa fever is commonly reported. Laboratory studies demonstrated that the highly lethal Zaire Ebola virus is responsible for the outbreak.
As a result of the EVD outbreak, the government of Sierra Leone a public state of emergency declaring that all dead bodies should be buried by the burial teams, without washing and in body bags. This declaration is still in place as there are still new recorded cases of Ebola in the country.
CAFOD is implementing the Safe and Dignified Burial project in the Kambia district which is aimed at providing Safe and Dignified medical Burials to dead bodies in the entire district.
To date, CAFOD has trained and is supporting burials teams and grave diggers and burial liaison officers in Kambia district. The burial teams have conducted over 2000 burials from the beginning of the project to date. However these teams are yet to receive a robust and well-structured Psycho Social support to enable them to be more energised and mentally fit to be effective and efficient whiles conducting burials.
